data.name: Secret of the Rendrasha Blade CH1&2
data.detailed_description:
Ashar decides to embark on a journey to discover the true fate of his father, a legendary war hero, but an unimaginable destiny calls out to him, and he soon gets wrapped up into a tale of adventure that is far beyond anything anyone could have ever imagined.

Fun Features

• A classic JRPG with a twist! Modern concepts and techniques have been baked into the genre's play style.

• A threat system that allows you the option of customizing your party to funnel enemy damage towards a beefy tank character via taunts and other fun mechanics.

• There is a class system in place that lets you play the game in many different ways each offering their own unique play style. Become an impenetrable wall that makes powerful sword blows feel like fun noodles, or a mystical spell slinger that melts the face off anyone foolish enough to challenge you.

• Enjoy an intricate gathering & crafting system that allows you to craft many different armors, weapons, & potions to further customize your experience.

• A meaningful fishing system that provides buffs and quick use items in combat.

• A Night and day system that affects the world in a meaningful way.

• Tons & tons of secrets! bosses, puzzles, dungeons, & quests that give you powerful items and access to hidden lore.

The game had to be cut in half due to Development issues. I humbly Apologize to anyone this affects. The other half may come out as dlc or just simply a patch at some point.

reviews.review:
This review is after 15 hours of gameplay.  I will update it as I continue playing the game.

If I had to compare this game to another game I would say it would be Last Dream, but with more story.

[b]Overall - 8[/b]

[b]Gameplay - 9[/b]

1. [b]Choices[/b] - The game gives you a lot of dialogue / situational choices which is an unusal thing for an rpg maker game.  I am not sure how many of them have wide consequences, but after having tried a few different options for a few of them there are consequences to what you choose.  I totally did not steal that old ladies thread.

2. [b]Crafting[/b] - There are a ton of crafting recipes in the game.  I currently have 249 / 7056.  You gather a lot of resources out in the world and from mobs so most of my gear is crafted.  Despite there being so many recipes it hasn't felt overwhelming and gives you goals to achieve.

3. [b]Gear customization[/b] - Unlike Last Dream you don't choose to lv up stats or abilities, instead the stat / ability customization comes from slotting your gear with diffent types of augmentations / enchanting your gear.  Augmentations can be freely moved between gear while enchantments are non recoverable once you use them on gear.  Gear has a ton of slots and it feels like it will be quite a while before I fill all of them up.

4. [b]Classes[/b] - There are a lot of classes to choose from.  You can also change your class at any point in time which is nice if you find you don't like the one you chose or want a different play style.  Each class starts at lv 1 so you will have to level it up a bit if you change.


[b]Content - 9[/b]

1. [b]Dungeons[/b] - The caves, haunted mansions, forests, etc. are among some of the best I have seen.  They each have multiple mini events, mini bosses, and secrets to find.  The events often add to the story and provide some challenging bosses and good loot.

2. [b]Difficulty[/b] - The difficulty level feels just right.  You will run into multiple really tough side bosses which provide good goals to work towards beating.  Multiple times I thought I was super powerful after beating some side bosses and getting some awesome augments only to find another really tough boss which puts me in my place.  However that just makes it more fun to get even stronger.  Additionally the time of day can effect the difficulty of monsters in certain areas.  Night time will pump up some of the beasts and undead wandering the land, while not effecting monsters in caves for example.

3. [b]Open world-ness[/b] - There are a number of side quests to do and optional bosses / areas to find.  Once you get out of the first town area you get quite a bit of freedom to roam around.

4. [b]Exploration[/b] - The game rewards you for exploring.  You don't just find potions and basic junk while wandering around.  You will often find good recipes, powerful gear augments, and rare crafting materials.  Exploration is fun when you know there is always the potential to find something new and interesting.

[b]Story - 5[/b]

1. [b]Characters[/b] - You get the first 3 party members in quick succession and this left me feeling like I didn't get a chance to know anything about the personality or backstory of any of them.  I hope this improves as I get further into the story.  I mostly think of them by their class names rather than their character names which isn't a good sign.

2. [b]Main story[/b] - The main story is just average so far.  I know there are some bad guys and I am fighting against them, but I don't really know much about what is going on.  It feels like things are moving too fast without enough realistic justification or motivation for my characters to be handling this world saving quest.

3. [b]Conversations[/b] - The conversations where you have options to choose are interesting and give a great feel to some of the initial conversations especially in the first town.  However for the rest of the npc conversations where you pick topics to discuss with the npcs I quickly got the sense that each npc's answer to the questions was the same with a little different text.  This made me not interested in talking to npcs because I figured they had nothing new to tell me after asking the first npc the questions I had.  The game Eridia is the best example I know of where it is fun to talk to npcs.  It was the only rpg I have played where I looked forward to every npc conversation because the dialogue was funny and many npcs cause conversations between your own party members which developed their personalities as well.
